Exercise: Side Lying Groin Stretch

Category:
stretching

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
static

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- abduction
- unilateral_hip_adduction

Primary Muscles:

- adductors

Secondary Muscles:

- hamstrings

Equipment:
None

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.75

Energy Requirement:
low

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- improve_hip_flexibility
- relieve_lower_back_tension

Contraindications:

- acute hip or groin injury

Exercise Variations:
None

Substitution Options:
None

Instructions:

- Start off by lying on your right side and bend your right knee in front of you to stabilize the torso.
- Rest your head on your right hand or shoulder. Lift your left leg upward and hold it by the back of the knee (easier) or the foot (harder).
- Pull your left knee in toward your left shoulder and simultaneously press your foot or knee down to the floor. To intensify this stretch, straighten your left leg. Switch sides.
